properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 4:56AM EDT until October 11 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Western Rockingham County in north central North
Carolina...
Stokes County in north central North Carolina...
Southeastern Surry County in northwestern North Carolina...
Henry County in south central Virginia...
The City of Martinsville in south central Virginia...
Patrick County in southwestern Virginia...
Southern Franklin County in west central Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 456 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Rapid river
rises have already caused minor flooding in the advisory area.
Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Baker Branch, Belews Creek, Big Beaver Island Creek, Bassett
Branch, Archies Creek, Beaver Creek, Ararat River and Anglin
Branch. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected
over the area through 6 AM. This additional rain will result in
minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Eden, Martinsville, Rocky Mount, Wentworth, Mayodan, Madison and
Pilot Mountain.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather Service
by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports and
pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Rutherford, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 4:42AM EDT until October 11 at 6:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Rutherford County in western North Carolina...

* Until 645 AM EDT.

* At 442 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen, with additional torrential rainfall moving into the
warned area.  Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Rapid rises should be expected on area creeks and streams,
including along Cleghorn Creek in Rutherfordton, Floyds Creek near
Forest City, and Mountain Creek near Green Hill.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Forest City, Rutherfordton, Spindale, Ellenboro, Bostic, South
Mountains State Park, Alexander Mills, Sunshine, Union Mills and
Caroleen.

Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms will develop over the
next few hours and the threat will persist through the early morning
hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very efficient at
producing heavy rainfall.  Flash flooding is imminent or occurring
across the area. Caution is advised near any stream or other
vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain
develops. Please have a plan in place should you experience flash
flooding and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation
orders from Emergency Management officials.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 11 at 1:39AM PDT until October 12 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected. Short
period north-northwest wind waves will interact with a
building west-northwest long period swell.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM PDT early this morning through Monday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Spartanburg, SC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 4:26AM EDT until October 11 at 5:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Spartanburg County in upstate South Carolina...

* Until 530 AM EDT.

* At 426 AM EDT, a prolonged period of steady rainfall has produced
3-6 inches across Spartanburg County, saturating area soils and
causing isolated areas of nuisance flooding.  Additional rain may
move into the eastern part of the county, impacting Cross Anchor,
Enoree, and Pauline.

* Areas of greatest concern include along Lawsons Fork Creek and
Meadow Creek near Inman; the South Pacolet River, Motlow Creek, and
Holston Creek near Campobello; Bear Creek and Obed Creek north of
Lake Bowen; and areas near Croft State Park.  Earlier, Glendale
Fire Department reported nuisance flooding along Country Club Rd
near Church St.  Flood conditions there are likely to worsen.
Please obey all barricades and avoid flooded roadways.  Only a few
inches of water can strand your vehicle.

* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the
next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-
access areas, and  campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Spartanburg, Boiling Springs SC, Woodruff, Lyman, Pacolet, Cowpens,
Wellford, Inman, Mayo and Roebuck.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Buncombe, NC; Henderson, NC; Rutherford, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 4:11AM EDT until October 11 at 7:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Buncombe County in western North Carolina...
Northeastern Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Rutherford County in western North Carolina...

* Until 715 AM EDT.

* At 411 AM EDT, The Rocky Broad River near Bat Cave crested at 9.1
feet near midnight and has steadily fallen to 7.8 feet and will
continue a gradual recession below the Minor Flood Stage of 7.5
feet over the next hour, with the localized shallow flooding
observed along US 64 (Main St) near Dogwood RV park receding
shortly thereafter.  However, Lake Lure Dam continues to release
water downstream along the Broad River, with nuisance to Minor
impacts to low-lying areas near US 64.  Lake Lure releases will
likely end soon with conditions downstream improving. In the
meantime, a final round of heavy rainfall is approaching the
Chimney Rock/Lake Lure area.  At this time, the heavy rainfall is
not expected to exacerbate ongoing flooding.  Therefore, once this
heavy rain passes and floodwaters recede, the Flash Flood Warning
will be cancelled.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.   An isolated landslide or two cannot be ruled
out.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Hendersonville, Brevard, Columbus, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat
Rock, Etowah, Mountain Home, Laurel Park and Tryon.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
McDowell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 515 AM EDT.

* At 410 AM EDT, Rounds of torrential rainfall have impacted many
areas of McDowell County following a prolonged period of steady
light to moderate rain, which produced storm-total rainfall of 3-6
inches over the past 12 hours.  This rainfall over saturated soils
is causing more significant rises to develop along areas streams
and associated tributaries.  Areas of greatest concern include the
headwaters of Cove Creek and the Second Broad River near Sugar
Hill, where the 3300 block of Sugar Hill Road is closed due to
flooding; Nix Creek near Providence; Crooked Creek near Moffitt
Hill; and the Upper Catawba River between Old Fort and Pleasant
Gardens, including along Lytle Mountain Rd, where a foot of flood
waters have currently closed the roadway.  Additionally, a
landslide has been observed on NC-226A with minor impacts to the
roadway.  Additional areas of Minor flooding are expected to
develop over the next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and
heed all evacuation orders from local Emergency Management
officials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-
access areas, and campgrounds.  Low-lying roadways are
likely to be flooded.  An isolated landslide or two cannot

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 1:08AM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Elko NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall and debris flows
are possible.

* WHERE...Portions of eastern, northeast, and south central Nevada,
including the following areas, in eastern Nevada, White Pine. In
northeast Nevada, the Ruby Mountains and East Humboldt Range in
Elko, South Central Elko and Southeastern Elko. In south central
Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern Nye.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams,
and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. In addition, flash
flooding is possible over recently burned areas like the former
Ward Fire, Kearny Fire, Oxley Fire, Secret Pass Fire, Starr Valley
Fire, Jones Fire, and Egberts Fire. Other burn scar locations in
the watch area could also be affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture from decaying Hurricane Rachel is expected to move
northward, crossing into portions of east-central and eastern
Nevada late tonight through roughly Monday. This significant
moisture will interact with upper level low pressure to bring
widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms to the watch area.
Moderate to locally heavy rain will cause excessive runoff and
may result in rock, mud, and debris flows in and near former fire
burned areas, steep terrain, and poorly drained urban areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
